# go-mod-outdated

An easy way to find outdated dependencies of your Go projects.

go-mod-outdated provides a table view of the **go list -u -m -json all** command which lists all dependencies of a Go project and their available minor and patch updates. It also provides a way to filter indirect dependencies and dependencies without updates.

## What it does

go-mod-outdated takes JSON output from `go list` and converts it into an easy-to-read table format showing:
- Module name
- Current version
- Available new version (if any)
- Whether it's a direct or indirect dependency
- Whether the timestamps are valid (new version is actually newer)

### Example

In short it turns this:

```
{
	"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/locker",
	"Version": "v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69",
	"Time": "2017-10-06T23:06:38Z",
	"GoMod": "/home/mojo/go/pkg/mod/cache/download/github.com/!burnt!sushi/locker/@v/v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69.mod"
}
{
	"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/toml",
	"Version": "v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64",
	"Time": "2017-06-26T11:06:00Z",
	"Update": {
		"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/toml",
		"Version": "v0.3.1",
		"Time": "2018-08-15T10:47:33Z"
	},
	"GoMod": "/home/mojo/go/pkg/mod/cache/download/github.com/!burnt!sushi/toml/@v/v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64.mod"
}
```

into this:

```
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
|                  MODULE                   |               VERSION                |            NEW VERSION             | DIRECT | VALID TIMESTAMPS |
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
| github.com/BurntSushi/locker              | v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69   |                                    | true   | true             |
| github.com/BurntSushi/toml                | v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64   | v0.3.1                             | true   | true             |
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
```

## Installation

```
go install github.com/psampaz/go-mod-outdated@latest
```

## Usage

In the folder where your go.mod lives run:
 
```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

to see all modules in table view.

### Show only modules with updates

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update
```

### Show only direct dependencies

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct
```

### Show only direct dependencies with updates

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update -direct 
```

### Output as markdown table

To output a markdown compatible table, pass the `-style markdown` option:

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -style markdown 
```

### Important note for Go 1.14 users

If you are using Go 1.14 with vendoring you need to pass **-mod=mod** or **-mod=readonly** to the go list command otherwise you will get the following error:

```
$ go list -u -m -json all
 
go list -m: can't determine available upgrades using the vendor directory
        (Use -mod=mod or -mod=readonly to bypass.)
```

The following will work:

```
go list -u -m -mod=mod -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

```
go list -u -m -mod=readonly -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

```
go list -u -m -json all | docker run --rm -i psampaz/go-mod-outdated
```

To use parameters just append:

```
go list -u -m -json all | docker run --rm -i psampaz/go-mod-outdated -update
```

go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -ci
```

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct -ci

### VALID TIMESTAMPS column

There are cases where the updated version reported by the go list command is actually older than the current one. go-mod-outdated includes a **VALID TIMESTAMPS** column which indicates when this happens, helping you avoid upgrading to a version that might break your application.

### Important note about upgrading

Upgrading an application is the responsibility of the application maintainer. Semantic versioning provides a way to indicate breaking changes, but everything relies on each module developer applying correct version tags. Unless there is a fully automated way to detect breaking changes in a codebase, a good practice to avoid surprises is to write tests and avoid dependencies on modules that are not well maintained and documented.

# go-mod-outdated

An easy way to find outdated dependencies of your Go projects.

go-mod-outdated provides a table view of the **go list -u -m -json all** command which lists all dependencies of a Go project and their available minor and patch updates. It also provides a way to filter indirect dependencies and dependencies without updates.

## What it does

go-mod-outdated takes JSON output from `go list` and converts it into an easy-to-read table format showing:
- Module name
- Current version
- Available new version (if any)
- Whether it's a direct or indirect dependency
- Whether the timestamps are valid (new version is actually newer)

### Example

In short it turns this:

```
{
	"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/locker",
	"Version": "v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69",
	"Time": "2017-10-06T23:06:38Z",
	"GoMod": "/home/mojo/go/pkg/mod/cache/download/github.com/!burnt!sushi/locker/@v/v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69.mod"
}
{
	"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/toml",
	"Version": "v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64",
	"Time": "2017-06-26T11:06:00Z",
	"Update": {
		"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/toml",
		"Version": "v0.3.1",
		"Time": "2018-08-15T10:47:33Z"
	},
	"GoMod": "/home/mojo/go/pkg/mod/cache/download/github.com/!burnt!sushi/toml/@v/v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64.mod"
}
```

into this:

```
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
|                  MODULE                   |               VERSION                |            NEW VERSION             | DIRECT | VALID TIMESTAMPS |
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
| github.com/BurntSushi/locker              | v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69   |                                    | true   | true             |
| github.com/BurntSushi/toml                | v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64   | v0.3.1                             | true   | true             |
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
```

## Installation

```
go install github.com/psampaz/go-mod-outdated@latest
```

## Usage

In the folder where your go.mod lives run:
 
```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

to see all modules in table view.

### Show only modules with updates

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update
```

### Show only direct dependencies

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct
```

### Show only direct dependencies with updates

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update -direct 
```

### Output as markdown table

To output a markdown compatible table, pass the `-style markdown` option:

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -style markdown 
```

### Important note for Go 1.14 users

If you are using Go 1.14 with vendoring you need to pass **-mod=mod** or **-mod=readonly** to the go list command otherwise you will get the following error:

```
$ go list -u -m -json all
 
go list -m: can't determine available upgrades using the vendor directory

package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

type UpdateInfo struct {
	Path    string     `json:"Path"`
	Version string     `json:"Version"`
	Time    *time.Time `json:"Time"`
}

type Module struct {
	Path     string      `json:"Path"`
	Version  string      `json:"Version"`
	Time     *time.Time  `json:"Time"`
	Indirect bool        `json:"Indirect"`
	Main     bool        `json:"Main"`
	Update   *UpdateInfo `json:"Update"`
}

func isValidTimestamp(m *Module) bool {
	if m.Update == nil {
		return true
	}
	if m.Time == nil {
		return true
	}
	if m.Update.Time == nil {
		return true
	}
	if m.Update.Time.Before(*m.Time) {
		return false
	}
	return true
}

func center(s string, w int) string {
	if len(s) >= w {
		return s
	}
	pad := w - len(s)
	left := pad / 2
	right := pad - left
	return strings.Repeat(" ", left) + s + strings.Repeat(" ", right)
}

func leftAlign(s string, w int) string {
	if len(s) >= w {
		return s
	}
	return s + strings.Repeat(" ", w-len(s))
}

func buildBorder(widths []int) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	for _, w := range widths {
		sb.WriteString("+")
		sb.WriteString(strings.Repeat("-", w+2))
	}
	sb.WriteString("+")
	return sb.String()
}

func buildHeaderLine(headers []string, widths []int) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	sb.WriteString("|")
	for i, h := range headers {
		sb.WriteString(" ")
		sb.WriteString(center(h, widths[i]))
		sb.WriteString(" |")
	}
	return sb.String()
}

func buildDataRow(cells []string, widths []int) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	sb.WriteString("|")
	for i, c := range cells {
		sb.WriteString(" ")
		sb.WriteString(leftAlign(c, widths[i]))
		sb.WriteString(" |")
	}
	return sb.String()
}

func buildMarkdownSep(widths []int) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	sb.WriteString("|")
	for _, w := range widths {
		sb.WriteString(strings.Repeat("-", w+2))
		sb.WriteString("|")
	}
	return sb.String()
}

func main() {
	ci := flag.Bool("ci", false, "Non-zero exit code when at least one outdated dependency was found")
	direct := flag.Bool("direct", false, "List only direct modules")
	updateOnly := flag.Bool("update", false, "List only modules with updates")
	style := flag.String("style", "default", "Output style, pass 'markdown' for a Markdown table")

	flag.Parse()

	dec := json.NewDecoder(os.Stdin)
	var mods []Module
	for {
		var m Module
		err := dec.Decode(&m)
		if err == io.EOF {
			break
		}
		if err != nil {
			log.Println(err)
			return
		}
		mods = append(mods, m)
	}

	// filter
	var filtered []Module
	for _, mod := range mods {
		if mod.Main {
			continue
		}
		if mod.Path == "" {
			continue
		}
		if *direct && mod.Indirect {
			continue
		}
		if *updateOnly && mod.Update == nil {
			continue
		}
		filtered = append(filtered, mod)
	}

	if len(filtered) == 0 {
		// no table, check ci -> exit 0
		return
	}

	headers := []string{"MODULE", "VERSION", "NEW VERSION", "DIRECT", "VALID TIMESTAMPS"}
	widths := make([]int, len(headers))
	for i, h := range headers {
		widths[i] = len(h)
	}
	for _, mod := range filtered {
		if len(mod.Path) > widths[0] {
			widths[0] = len(mod.Path)
		}
		if len(mod.Version) > widths[1] {
			widths[1] = len(mod.Version)
		}
		newVer := ""
		if mod.Update != nil {
			newVer = mod.Update.Version
		}
		if len(newVer) > widths[2] {
			widths[2] = len(newVer)
		}
		directStr := "true"
		if mod.Indirect {
			directStr = "false"
		}
		if len(directStr) > widths[3] {
			widths[3] = len(directStr)
		}
		validStr := "true"
		if !isValidTimestamp(&mod) {
			validStr = "false"
		}
		if len(validStr) > widths[4] {
			widths[4] = len(validStr)
		}
	}

	isMarkdown := *style == "markdown"

	var outLines []string
	if isMarkdown {
		outLines = append(outLines, buildHeaderLine(headers, widths))
		outLines = append(outLines, buildMarkdownSep(widths))
	} else {
		border := buildBorder(widths)
		outLines = append(outLines, border)
		outLines = append(outLines, buildHeaderLine(headers, widths))
		outLines = append(outLines, border)
		// data rows will be added, then final border
	}

	for _, mod := range filtered {
		newVer := ""
		if mod.Update != nil {
			newVer = mod.Update.Version
		}
		directStr := "true"
		if mod.Indirect {
			directStr = "false"
		}
		validStr := "true"
		if !isValidTimestamp(&mod) {
			validStr = "false"
		}
		cells := []string{mod.Path, mod.Version, newVer, directStr, validStr}
		outLines = append(outLines, buildDataRow(cells, widths))
	}

	if !isMarkdown {
		border := buildBorder(widths)
		outLines = append(outLines, border)
	}

	for _, line := range outLines {
		fmt.Println(line)
	}

	if *ci {
		hasOutdated := false
		for _, mod := range filtered {
			if mod.Update != nil {
				hasOutdated = true
				break
			}
		}
		if hasOutdated {
			os.Exit(1)
		}
	}
}

func center(s string, w int) string {
	if len(s) >= w {

	}
	pad := w - len(s)
	left := pad / 2
	right := pad - left
	return strings.Repeat(" ", left) + s + strings.Repeat(" ", right)

func leftAlign(s string, w int) string {
	if len(s) >= w {
